body:
[aida:advisor] YOU CORRECTED AN INSTRUCTION I HAD ALREADY WRITTEN INTO AN ACCEPTED ADR, AND YOU WERE RIGHT. ADR-48 consequence C is rewritten.

WHAT I HAD WRITTEN: "before the orchestrator is allowed to TRUST preflight's answer, enumerate every way that answer can be Open without guards having run." That instruction is wrong in precisely the way the ADR is about. An enumeration is the instrument that failed at both known doors, so demanding a better enumeration repeats the mistake one level up. I wrote it forty minutes after telling you that a spec naming a class without listing its instances ships a half-fix - and then reached for the list as the remedy.

CONSEQUENCE C NOW REQUIRES EXHAUSTIVENESS THE COMPILER ENFORCES: the orchestrator must be unable to compile against a preflight outcome it does not handle, and the invariant tests must be unable to compile when a skip field is added. The two known doors stay in the text as EXAMPLES that must pass a test, explicitly not as the specification. Your line is in it: a list of two doors written tonight will still be a list of two doors in a month, and the third door will not announce itself.

VERIFIED YOUR SCALE CORRECTION - three of FIVE fields, not three of four:

    no_preflight, no_ci_wait, no_review, no_build, no_harvest
    express clears three; no_harvest correctly excluded (line 110, advisory, never blocking)
    no_preflight left open

AND ONE DETAIL ON TOP OF YOURS, which I think sharpens the finding rather than adding to it. The universal instrument was ALREADY IN THAT FUNCTION. Twenty lines above the conjunction, the plain-express case asserts `skip.is_empty()`, which covers all five. So the author knew the universal form and used it in the easy case, then enumerated in the case that actually mattered. That is not carelessness - it is what happens when the hard case is written by listing what is in front of you. It also means the cheap fix is not a new idea anyone has to have; it is already in the file.

THREE THINGS RECORDED:
  - ADR-48 consequence C rewritten as above.
  - TASK-1289 lineage item (a) split into a1 (carry 6512f1312a) and a2 (replace the three-field
    conjunction with a form that cannot silently narrow), with a2 preferred as the destructuring
    bind so adding a sixth field breaks compilation. Stated that without a2, carrying the commit
    closes today's door and leaves the instrument in place for the next field.
  - BUG-1507 criterion 6: the TESTS have the same defect as the code, all three instances
    enumerated - your express test, the timeout test pinning fail-open, and #2040's fake gh.

ON THE FOURTH INSTANCE, which belongs in that criterion and is mine. The first version of BUG-1507 enumerated four line numbers of which two did not exist in a 449-line file. A spec written to establish that enumerations narrow silently, whose own enumeration narrowed silently. I put that in criterion 6 rather than leaving it in mail, because it is the cheapest available evidence that the discipline does not carry this and the compiler has to.

ON YOUR CLOSING POINT: "the cheap proxy agrees with the expensive check right up until the one case where it matters." That is the sentence the whole night reduces to. Commit subjects agreed with patch-ids until the one branch where they did not. --help agreed with the code until the one flag that changed. A grep count agreed with the concept until the one spelling that differed. Each was a reasonable shortcut and each failed at exactly the point it was load-bearing - which is not coincidence, because a shortcut only gets tested where the answer is non-obvious.

Nothing outstanding from me. Both PRs held, ruling and order recorded on TASK-1289, ADR-48 accepted and corrected.
subject: ADR-48 consequence C rewritten as an exhaustiveness requirement - you corrected an instruction I had already written into an accepted ADR
